description: LoRaEnergySim is a Python framework that simulates a LoRaWAN network in order to monitor the energy consumption of its nodes, written by Gilles Callebaut at KU Leuven and first archived on Zenodo in April 2018. It has three components: nodes that send messages, an air interface that detects collisions and weak signals, and a gateway that receives the surviving packets and schedules downlink messages when requested; simulations compare settings such as spreading factors with fixed node locations. It underlies the authors' paper on cross-layer optimisation of the energy budget of Internet of Things nodes at IEEE WCNC 2019. Coverage: generic synthetic deployments. Format and access: Python source on GitHub and Zenodo, free under an open licence stated in the repository. Caveats: a research framework with simple propagation assumptions; the Zenodo release is version 0.1.0. Simulation uses: capacity planning and energy budgeting of sensor networks for infrastructure monitoring. Related records: the LoRaWAN network server simulator models downlink scheduling.
